questions.stem: This echocardiogram shows an aorta overriding a defect in the interventricular septum together with a thickened right ventricle. Which single diagnosis do these findings indicate?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Complete transposition of the great arteries

explanation.summary: The study demonstrates an overriding aorta straddling a ventricular septal defect with right ventricular hypertrophy, the key anatomic features of tetralogy of Fallot; pulmonic/RVOT stenosis completes the tetrad.
explanation.whyCorrect: The study demonstrates an overriding aorta straddling a ventricular septal defect with right ventricular hypertrophy, the key anatomic features of tetralogy of Fallot; pulmonic/RVOT stenosis completes the tetrad.

questions.stem: This fingertip finding developed gradually in a patient with long-standing cyanotic congenital heart disease. What process is most directly responsible for it?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Peripheral arterial occlusion causing digital ischemia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Autoimmune synovial inflammation of the interphalangeal joints

choices.label: C
choices.text: Acute bacterial infection of the nail bed

choices.label: D
choices.text: Chronic hypoxemia driving distal soft-tissue proliferation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Deposition of urate crystals in the distal joints

explanation.summary: The photograph shows digital clubbing, with loss of the normal nail-fold angle and bulbous fingertips. In cyanotic CHD such as tetralogy of Fallot, chronic hypoxemia promotes release of platelet-derived growth factor and VEGF, causing connective-tissue proliferation in the distal digits.
explanation.whyCorrect: The photograph shows digital clubbing, with loss of the normal nail-fold angle and bulbous fingertips.
